outcomes.text: Explain the main ideas in Content clauses and reported speech.
Recognise the patterns in real sentences.
Use the ideas when you read and write.

key_terms.definition: A clause that characteristically functions as dependent within a larger construction.
A clause that functions as head of the construction containing it.
A clause headed by a primary verb form, including subjunctive clauses.
A clause headed by a gerund-participle, past participle or infinitival plain form.
The default class of finite subordinate clause, lacking the special properties of relative and comparative clauses.
A content clause with declarative clause type.
A content clause with closed or open interrogative type.
A content clause with exclamative type, based on what or how.
A marker such as that, whether or if that introduces a subordinate clause.
A declarative content clause introduced by that.
A declarative content clause without that.
A declarative content clause whose governing item excludes that.
Placement of a clause after dummy it rather than in subject position.
A construction expressing requirement or recommendation, often with a subjunctive or should.
A finite clause construction using the plain form, as in that he be told.
A past-tense form used to mark modal remoteness rather than past time.
The residual mood form were used in hypothetical or counterfactual clauses.
The property of a predicate that treats its complement as factive, presupposing its truth.
A construction expressing doubt about a question or its answer.
A subordinator introducing closed interrogative content clauses.
A conditional preposition or subordinator; in content clauses it introduces interrogatives only under restricted conditions.
A conditional construction quantifying over a set of alternatives, such as whether he comes or not.
The reporting of another utterance, either directly or indirectly.
A report of what was said using a content clause, often with backshift and deixis shifts.
A report that quotes the original utterance.
A blend of indirect report and the original speaker’s perspective or wording.
The use of past tense in reported speech to mark anteriority relative to the report.
The adjustment of pronouns, time and place expressions in indirect report.

opening.prompt: Which clause is a content clause?

options.text: that she is right in He knows that she is right
options.feedback: It is a declarative content clause complement of knows.

opening.prompt: Which clause type is I wonder what he does?

options.feedback: It contains the interrogative phrase what.
Imperative content clauses do not occur.

opening.prompt: Why is that obligatory in That they were lying is obvious?

options.text: The content clause is subject and precedes the matrix predicator.
options.feedback: The marker signals the subordinate clause at the start.
The matrix predicate is be + obvious.

options.text: know in I know that she left
believe in I believe that she left
say in I say that she left
The use of a past tense to mark anteriority relative to the report
options.feedback: It is a perspective shift in reported speech.

closing.prompt: Why is there no inversion in I wonder what he does?

options.text: It is a subordinate interrogative, which normally has subject-predicator order.
options.feedback: Main-clause questions invert; subordinate interrogatives usually do not.

closing.prompt: Why is that impossible in Who does she think is the ringleader?

options.text: The subject of the content clause is a gap linked to who.
options.feedback: That cannot intervene between the gap and its antecedent.
The content clause is declarative in form.

closing.prompt: What is that they were lying in It is obvious that they were lying?

options.feedback: Dummy it fills the subject position.
The clause is not optional scene-setting.

closing.prompt: Why is whether possible but if excluded in We discussed whether to go?

options.text: Whether can follow a preposition; if cannot.

closing.prompt: Which feature is characteristic of direct reported speech?

options.text: It retains the original speaker’s deictic centre.
options.feedback: I, now and here refer to the original utterance.
Direct report quotes rather than taking a that-clause.
Direct report is not normally backshifted.
